item.title: The Limits and Duties of the Distant Observer
item.description: Living abroad does not disqualify a person from judging foreign affairs, and the demand that an émigré keep silent is censorship dressed up as humility. But the freedom to analyze from a distance carries duties: deferring where competence ends, taking a side without lying, diagnosing rather than commanding, and answering for the effect that analysis has on the world it describes.
